LESSON: SIGN READING 3.4.1 INTENSIVE SIGN READING: POETRY

Grade: SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade seven
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 3
Topic 3.4: Sign Reading 3.4.1 Intensive Sign Reading: Poetry
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Sign Reading 3.4.1 Intensive Sign Reading: Poetry, part of Strand 3 in SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade seven ENGLISH.

Key inquiry question: How can one tell a text is a poem? 2. How can one sign read a poem?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Sign Reading 3.4.1 Intensive Sign Reading: Poetry together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Digital literacy: Learner develops the skill of connecting using technology as they use digital devices to search sources online for

different poems and note the titles and the poets, while observing integrity and cyber safety.

● Citizenship: Learner develops the skill of ethical digital citizenship as they search online for appropriate and relevant content.

Values:
● Integrity: is achieved as learners utilise the digital resources prudently to source online or offline for poems.

Link to other subjects

The learner is able to relate the concept of intensive reading of poetry to their learning Creative arts and Religious Education
